items.title: Are Value and Momentum Still Everywhere?
items.summary: I became insane, with long intervals of horrible sanity. – Edgar Allan Poe (1) We have long regarded value and momentum as the “varsity” factors in stock selection.
items.finding: Decades of academic research, including our own, have shown that, historically, buying cheap stocks and buying winners has been associated with higher average returns.

items.title: Scenarios for future banking: implications for profitability, liquidity and solvency
items.summary: Who will perform banking’s core functions a decade from now, and how will risks and profitability evolve?
items.finding: Our framework structures expert judgement rather than forecasts.

items.title: The Cross-section of Subjective Expectations: Understanding Prices and Anomalies
items.summary: We decompose cross-sectional differences in the level of price-earnings ratios using professional forecasts.
items.finding: High price-earnings ratios are accounted for by both low expected returns and overly high expected earnings growth.

items.title: AI‑enabled Investor Sentiment Analysis and Stock Market Prediction
items.publisher: International Journal of Finance and Investment
items.venue: International Journal of Finance and Investment
items.summary: The efficient market hypothesis assumes that investors have complete rationality, while traditional theories advocate that stock prices are determined by the fundamentals of the enterprise.
items.finding: However, these methods have insufficient accuracy and poor timeliness, and cannot capture retail public opinion in real time, explain frequent stock price fluctuations and various market anomalies in the stock market.

items.title: Layered framing: Warren Buffett’s shareholder letters, essays and four Korean editions
items.summary: This study traces the framing of Warren Buffett’s shareholder letters across five phases in two parts: their compilation as The Essays of Warren Buffett (1997) and four Korean editions (2001–2022).
items.finding: Within editions, naming, arrangement and lexis need not align uniformly, as each is oriented toward legitimacy under distinct, level-specific field expectations.

items.title: FinTech Adoption, Bank Profitability, and Stability: The Mediating Role of Operational Cost Efficiency in Bangladesh's Commercial Banking Sector
items.summary: While financial technology (FinTech) is seen as a contributor to bank performance, the empirical evidence of digitization's ability to translate into improved profit and stability outcomes and efficiency gains, within emerging systems dominated by banks is not conclusive.
items.finding: The adoption of FinTech presents no significant relationship with profitability, stability or cost efficiency, while cost efficiency does not significantly transmit the effect of FinTech to either outcome.

items.title: Interdependence and Contagion Between Crude Oil Bubbles and Chinese Stock Market Bubbles
items.summary: Studying the interdependence and contagion effects between crude oil bubbles and China’s stock market bubble provides a cross-market perspective for monitoring risks across markets and regulating bubbles.
items.finding: The results show multiple bubbles in crude oil and Chinese stock markets, accompanied by excessive market volatility.

items.title: The Anthropic Feedback Loop: The Cost of Capital Delusion and Diversion!
items.summary: I knew that my post on Anthropic would draw strong reactions, when I made it public last week.
items.finding: This reframing allows me to add a few details that I might have glossed over in my last post, as well as correct errors (none of which thankfully changed by value estimate: Value per share : Though I have a share count, created by adding the shares reported…

items.title: Forward Return Expectations
items.summary: We measure investors’ short- and long-term stock-return expectations using both options and survey data.
items.finding: The excess variation in forward return expectations can help account for a meaningful share of the stock-price declines during the global financial crisis and the COVID-19 crisis.

items.title: A Conditional Shrinkage Method for Portfolio Selection
items.summary: We develop a conditional shrinkage method for portfolio selection.
items.finding: We implement the method using investor sentiment and find that the estimated relation predominantly leads to greater shrinkage toward 1/N when sentiment is low, improving mean-variance efficiency while maintaining low turnover.

items.title: Factor Investing in the Age of the Magnificent Seven
When Factors Sleep and Wake: The Dynamic Nature of Factor Investing in US and European Investment-Grade Credit
Artificial Intelligence and Global Transformations in Dividend Policy: Contemporary Trends and Structural Changes
items.summary: This study investigates the contemporary trends and structural transformations in dividend policy in the context of artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy, and global economic transformation.
items.finding: The findings reveal that dividend policy has evolved beyond its traditional role as a profit distribution mechanism into a comprehensive strategic instrument for shareholder value creation and corporate financial management.

items.title: Investor Sentiment and Stock Price Dynamics: An Empirical Study on the Casablanca Stock Exchange
items.venue: Journal d’Economie, de Management, d’Environnement et de Droit
items.summary: This study explores investor sentiment, a key concept in behavioral finance, reflecting the collective optimism or pessimism of market participants about future investments.
items.finding: As for the positive sentiment, it has an opposite effect compared to the negative one, it increases the return and reduces the risk.

items.title: The sustainable competitive advantage in the digital economy: value creation versus value recognition
items.summary: This study aims to investigate the competitive advantage in the digital economy, focusing on the Standard & Poor’s (Standard & Poor’s Financial Services (S&P) 500 companies.
items.finding: Originality/value The significance of the EVA is particularly evident when considering the competitive advantage of businesses operating at the core of the emergent digital economy and the integration of business and investment strategies in pursuit of…

items.title: Is Informed Short Selling Concentrated in Family Firms? Evidence from a Reinvestigation
items.summary: ABSTRACT We reinvestigate Anderson, Reeb, and Zhao's findings that informed short selling is unique to family firms and driven by information leakage from internal disputes.
items.finding: We also find no significant difference in abnormal short selling before negative earnings announcements.

items.title: The DNA of neuroticism and financial decisions
items.summary: A polygenic score (PGS) capturing genetic predisposition toward neuroticism predicts heterogeneity in risk aversion, return beliefs, and stock market participation.
items.finding: These characteristics serve as key channels through which the genetic propensity for neuroticism shapes financial choices.

items.title: The integrated effects of accounting measurement challenges on the representation of the intrinsic value of the economic entity
items.summary: This study aims to examine the individual effects of five fundamental challenges in accounting measurement, namely conceptual constraints, bias in professional judgment, the measurement of intangible assets, opportunistic managerial behavior, and rebound investor behavior, on accounting measurement.
items.finding: This variable constitutes the most influential factor in distorting intrinsic value, followed by rebound investor behavior (manifested as herding behavior) resulting from the loss of information quality.

items.title: Understanding Individual Investment Decisions Through Behavioral Biases: Evidence from Morocco
items.summary: Investment decisions involve a series of choices that can significantly affect the performance of financial investments.
items.finding: The findings reveal five underlying behavioral dimensions associated with individual investors’ investment decisions.

items.title: Large Funds and Corporate Bond Market Fragility
items.summary: The corporate bond fund industry is characterized by a high concentration of capital, with a substantial portion of assets managed by large funds.
items.finding: Exploring the underlying mechanisms, we find that large funds are more likely to reach for yield by holding illiquid bonds.

items.title: Financial Intermediary Relationships and Public Market Access
items.summary: Financial markets depend on more than capital, information, and investment opportunities.
items.finding: The authors find that disruptions to established underwriter relationships reduce venture capital fund multiples by approximately 7.8%.

items.title: Local Returns and Beliefs about the Stock Market
items.summary: We show that investors extrapolate from recent stock returns of locally headquartered firms when forming beliefs about aggregate stock market outcomes.
items.finding: Our findings suggest that beliefs about information contained in public signals vary systematically with geography, and are an important component of local biases in equity markets.

items.title: Managing through Factor Droughts: Benchmarks, Attribution, and Governance
Interpretable Allocation and Model-Predictive Rebalancing of Equity Portfolios, Tested on Real and Synthetic Markets
items.summary: A live equity portfolio poses three problems: which stocks to hold, when to trade, and whether the strategy holds up beyond the observed market.
items.finding: A market hedge that tightened a beta cap as the market weakened cost wealth on real prices but paid off in the most sustained simulated declines, and the generator's persistent trends favored score-based selection more than the real market did, which suggests…

items.title: Unintended Consequences of Holding Dollar Assets
items.summary: ABSTRACT We propose and examine a novel mechanism whereby holdings of dollar assets by foreign institutions can have a large, unexpected impact on foreign Treasury yields in crisis periods.
items.finding: We show that during the recent COVID crisis, U.K. institutions with substantial dollar holdings and FX hedging positions sold large amounts of gilts, contributing significantly to the observed gilt yield spike.

items.title: Conditioning Factor Exposure on Economic Regimes: Evidence from Momentum Investing
Specification LASSO and a Flexible Characteristics-Based Asset Pricing Model
items.summary: This paper studies a partially linear semiparametric additive model that allows for interactions among variables in high-dimensional settings.
items.finding: Empirically, we apply S-LASSO to a characteristics-based asset pricing model, exploring the linear and nonlinear effects of asset-specific characteristics on cross-sectional returns, as well as their interactions with firm size.

items.title: Europeans really don’t like to invest in stocks
items.summary: It has become a trope to say that there is no equity investment culture in continental Europe (at least nowhere near what we see in the Anglo-Saxon world).
items.finding: A new study shows that even if people win the lottery or gain a similar windfall, they may invest more in stocks, but the majority of households still won’t touch stocks.

items.title: Wall Street's most hated stocks are faring far better than its favorites
Short-Term Market Moves Won’t Give Us the Answers on AI
items.summary: Being an investor in an environment dominated by a highly consequential yet uncertain theme is exhausting.
items.finding: Everyone is searching for answers about the impact of AI and acting as if the next lurch higher or lower in the ‘AI trade’ might be the signal they have been waiting for.

items.title: How Many Americans Are Millionaires?
items.summary: If it feels like there are more millionaires in the U.S. than ever before, you're right.
items.finding: This means that only around 28% of millionaires are millionaires based on their liquid net worth alone.

items.title: The Role of SEBI in Protecting Investors in the Indian Stock Market
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
items.summary: Investor confidence is the foundation on which every securities market rests.
items.finding: It contends, however, that the concentration of functions, slow adjudication and the persistent vulnerability of retail investors call for continued reform, and it assesses the Securities Markets Code, 2025 against that need.

items.title: Women are their own enemies
items.summary: One of the things I observe with many women I work with is that they tend to be more reluctant to self-promote.
items.finding: But what this experiment shows is that women can be their own worst enemies by not promoting their work.

items.title: China is decoupling from the West
items.summary: Ever since the trade war between the US and China started in 2018, the mantra of Western businesses has been to decouple from China and reduce their dependency on Chinese goods.
items.finding: The charts below show how China’s imports of iron and steel (left-hand chart) and nickel (right-hand chart) have changed rapidly, particularly after the pandemic when the West implemented economic sanctions against Russia and became more focused on decoupling…

items.title: On AI and Iran, Trump risks bombing himself in the foot
items.summary: OK, oil prices are dropping rapidly, but do you really believe that the US will not bomb Iran after the midterms?
items.finding: I don’t and the resulting higher oil prices may have all kinds of unintended consequences.

items.title: The Greatest Sentence Ever Written by Walter Isaacson
items.summary: Get the Book: Print | eBook Walter Isaacson dissects the second sentence of the Declaration of Independence, gives background on the editing process from first draft to final form, and explains the meaning behind the words.
